grounded_facts: Moretti speaks to Sonny on the phone, positioning himself as the controlling authority and urging compliance.
memories.memory_text: I spoke to Sonny on the phone, positioning myself as the one in control and urging him to comply with my instructions to avoid escalation.

memories.memory_text: I was already on scene at the bank when the FBI showed up, and I knew we had suspects inside who might have hostages, so we were locking things down.

memories.memory_text: I saw Sonny being cheered by the crowd after the police lowered their weapons, and he started performing, turning to the cameras and waving.

grounded_facts: Sonny turns to cameras and waves, playing to the media and crowd after gaining symbolic victory.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Sonny realize his power in the moment and begin playing to the media, turning his profile to the cameras with a grin.

memories.memory_text: I witnessed Sylvia decide to reenter the bank despite being told to stay out, showing she was still committed to the hostages inside.

memories.memory_text: I was at the bank during an ongoing crisis with hostages, law enforcement responding, and a crowd gathering outside that started applauding and screaming when they realized what was happening.

grounded_facts: An ongoing armed standoff at a bank where Sonny and accomplices are holding hostages, with police negotiation and media presence.
memories.memory_text: I was standing there eating an ice cream bar when I saw the chaos unfold around the ongoing bank standoff, where Sal demanded to see Sonny and Sonny started shouting about needing a helicopter and a jet to escape.

grounded_facts: Sonny demands a helicopter and a large international jet with specific amenities to facilitate escape, marking a strategic escalation in his negotiation stance.
memories.memory_text: I heard Sonny demand a helicopter and a large international jet with a bar and a piano lounge to get out of the country, which marked a serious escalation in his escape plans.

grounded_facts: Sonny demands that his wife be brought to the bank, introducing a personal stake into the negotiation and potentially altering leverage dynamics.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sonny insisting that I bring his wife to the bank, making it clear she was now part of the negotiation.

memories.memory_text: I proposed trading Sonny's wife for the female hostages, trying to establish a quid pro quo that might move the negotiation forward.

grounded_facts: An ongoing hostage situation at a bank where Sonny negotiates with police led by Moretti.
memories.memory_text: I was leading the police response during the hostage situation at the bank, negotiating with Sonny, who shouted at me from inside, demanding to know what I was doing back there.

memories.memory_text: I saw Sonny hand the rifle to Sal and say he was going outside to confront me.

memories.memory_text: I told Sonny everything he asked for was on the way—his wife, a bus, the jet to Kennedy—trying to calm him down and keep him talking.

memories.memory_text: I heard Sonny ask for pizza, soft drinks, and aspirin for the hostages, and I confirmed we’d get it to them.

memories.memory_text: I saw Sonny turn and walk back into the bank after we finished talking.

memories.memory_text: I watched Sonny hand over a large sum from the bank's money to the delivery boy and say 'Keep the change,' making a show of it like some kind of twisted generosity.

memories.memory_text: I saw the tension at the bank entrance, with hostages inside, police surrounding the area, and a growing crowd of onlookers pressing close, all of us caught in the uncertainty of what would happen next.

memories.memory_text: I saw Sonny get angry at the crowd's greed, throw another bundle of money, and then laugh as people scrambled and fought over it.

memories.memory_text: I saw Sonny throw a wad of bills into the crowd, and I watched the chaos unfold as people scrambled, fought, and broke through barriers to grab the money, with even some cops joining in.

grounded_facts: Moretti nods ironically at Sonny after witnessing the crowd's chaotic reaction to the money throw.
memories.memory_text: After seeing the chaos, I nodded ironically at Sonny to acknowledge how absurd the whole scene had become.

memories.memory_text: I remember the Commissioner placing his hand over mine and massaging it fondly, a gesture that felt like a quiet acknowledgment of our shared history and the deep bond between us.

memories.memory_text: The Commissioner told me directly, 'Don't let 'em off the ground,' so I knew I was ordered to prevent the jet from taking off, no matter what it took.

memories.memory_text: I made it clear that I don't need institutional backing if I'm correct, but I do demand support if I happen to make an honest error.

grounded_facts: Moretti calls Sonny to inform him that his wife is being brought to the bank.
memories.memory_text: I called Sonny to tell him we were bringing in his wife.

memories.memory_text: I saw Sonny get alert after our call, hand his rifle to Sal, and leave the bank when he learned his wife was being brought in.

grounded_facts: The crowd greets Sonny with cheers as he appears at the bank door, showing public support.
memories.memory_text: I was moving with the others to intercept the police car when I saw Sonny appear at the bank door, and I heard the crowd erupt in cheers for him, though he kept his focus on the car.

memories.memory_text: I saw the driver of the police car get out and nod to me with a grin, acknowledging our connection as we coordinated on the scene.

memories.memory_text: I moved out into the street with Sheldon and the others to intercept the police car as it arrived and stopped at the corner, where the driver got out and nodded to me.

grounded_facts: A coordinated police operation unfolds as a marked car arrives through barricaded lines, engaging with key characters and introducing a new presence into the public standoff.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that this was a coordinated operation because the police car moved through the barricades with officers lifting them aside, and both the driver and another officer got out grinning, which suggested a planned and unified presence.

grounded_facts: Sonny's wife emerges from the police car, visibly disheveled but striking, marking a personal and emotional turning point in the scene.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sonny's wife get out of the police car, disheveled but striking, and I could feel the mood of the scene shift right then.

memories.memory_text: I saw Sonny calling out to Leon, shouting 'Leon! Happy Birthday!' a couple of times, but Leon didn't respond.

memories.memory_text: I was there when we took Leon toward the barbershop after he collapsed, trying to get him through the crowd quickly.

memories.memory_text: I helped the other detectives carry Leon toward the barbershop after he collapsed, even though I heard someone shouting—Sonny, I think—trying to reach him.

memories.memory_text: I saw Sonny rushing toward the bank and entering after we started taking Leon away and he didn't respond.

memories.memory_text: I was told that Sonny rushed into the bank and tried to get a phone to call me, showing how urgent it was.

grounded_facts: Sonny urgently asks to speak with a third party, showing concern.
memories.memory_text: I heard Sonny ask urgently if the person was all right and then insist, 'I want to talk to him,' showing how concerned he was.

memories.memory_text: I told Sonny the person was groggy and that I'd get him on his feet so he could call back later.

memories.memory_text: I was told that Sonny is holding people hostage in a bank because of the failed sex change operation and the troubled relationship with Leon.

memories.memory_text: I heard Leon recount how he tried to take his own life after realizing he would never get the sex change operation, due to deep depression and emotional turmoil.

grounded_facts: Leon reveals his gender identity struggle, failed marriage, and suicide attempt as context for Sonny's actions.
memories.memory_text: I learned from Leon about his gender identity struggle, his failed marriage, and his suicide attempt after realizing he wouldn't get the sex change operation, which he said was tied to Sonny's actions.

grounded_facts: A private, urgent conversation between Moretti and Leon in a barbershop, where Leon reveals the emotional and psychological roots of Sonny's hostage crisis.
memories.memory_text: I had a private and urgent conversation with Leon in a barbershop, where I pressed him to contact Sonny and end the hostage situation.

memories.memory_text: I told Leon he had to talk Sonny into giving himself up, making it clear he owed it to him and that he could be seen as an accessory if he didn't help.

grounded_facts: After failing to convince Leon to act, Moretti takes initiative to call Sonny at the bank directly.
memories.memory_text: I decided to take action myself and called Sonny directly from the wall phone after realizing Leon wouldn't do anything.

grounded_facts: Sonny acknowledges the media's focus on their sexuality but refuses to engage, calling it a 'freak show' and telling Sal to ignore it.
Sonny tells Sal he cannot control the media and should ignore the labels.
memories.memory_text: I heard Sonny tell Sal that the media calling them homosexuals didn't matter and that it was just a freak show they couldn't control, so he should ignore what they said.

grounded_facts: Sonny reacts to the sound of a passing jet with irritation, highlighting the absence of the promised escape aircraft.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sonny react with frustration to the sound of a passing jet, muttering to himself about how it was always flying overhead while their escape plane never came.

memories.memory_text: I realized the bank had lost main power because only the emergency lights were on inside, but I could still see lights across the street in the store windows.

memories.memory_text: I was told the phones in the bank were dead, so no one inside could reach me or call out.

grounded_facts: Moretti uses a bull-horn from outside to call Sonny to come out for a moment.
memories.memory_text: I used the bull-horn from outside to call Sonny, telling him to come out for a moment.

grounded_facts: An ongoing standoff at the bank during the night, involving hostages and law enforcement presence outside.
memories.memory_text: I was right in the middle of the standoff at the bank that night, with hostages inside and our team surrounding the building.

grounded_facts: Moretti uses a bull-horn from outside the bank to call for Sonny to come out.
memories.memory_text: I used the bull-horn to call out to Sonny, telling him to come out a minute so we could talk.

grounded_facts: A private discussion between Moretti and Sheldon in a barbershop at dusk/night.
memories.memory_text: I was in the barbershop with Sheldon at dusk, having a private conversation.

memories.memory_text: Sheldon told me that at 3:07 this became a federal matter and asked if he should take over, questioning whether I could keep control.

grounded_facts: Moretti makes a mocking comment about Sonny not seeing him, expressing contempt.

memories.memory_text: I saw Sheldon give me that smug, superior smile after my remark, like we both looked down on Sonny.

memories.memory_text: I witnessed the phone conversation between Sonny in the bank and Leon at the hospital, where Sonny demanded to know if I was listening and addressed me directly over the line.

memories.memory_text: I witnessed Sonny and Leon's emotional exchange where Leon confronted him about his talk of death, Sonny justified the robbery as being for Leon and invited him to escape, and they shared a final ironic goodbye.

grounded_facts: Sonny stamps out the burning register to prevent smoke from drawing outside attention.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sonny rush through the teller's gate and stamp out the burning register to stop the smoke from drawing attention.

grounded_facts: Sal aims his gun at the approaching man, ready to kill if he enters, showing eagerness for violence.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Sal raising his gun and aiming it at the man approaching the door, and from the way he was smiling and settling into position, I got the sense he was almost eager to shoot.

memories.memory_text: I was told that Mulvaney unlocked the door and convinced Sam, the insurance man, that the smoke was just from a cigarette in a wastebasket, and he managed to get him to leave without calling the police.

grounded_facts: Sonny ridicules Sylvia when she expresses fear of being locked in the vault.

grounded_facts: Sal checks his appearance, adjusting his tie and cuffs, showing careful preparation for the upcoming activity at the bank.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sal checking his tie and adjusting his cuffs in the car, getting himself ready for what was coming at the bank.

grounded_facts: Jackie emerges from the back of the car with a large florist box and hands it to Sonny.
Jackie hands the florist box to Sonny without verbal exchange, indicating a subordinate role.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jackie emerging from the back of the car with a large florist box and handing it to me without a word.

grounded_facts: Jackie exits the car, approaches the bank window, peers inside, and returns to report.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jackie get out of the car, walk to the bank window, peer inside, and then return.

grounded_facts: Jackie returns from the bank window and has a fake conversation with Sonny, likely conveying information.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jackie leaning in and having a fake conversation with me, likely passing along what he saw inside the bank.

grounded_facts: Sonny says 'seconds, Sal...' to signal that it is time for Sal to begin the operation.
memories.memory_text: I told Sal 'seconds, Sal...' to let him know it was time to begin the operation.

grounded_facts: A coordinated operation involving surveillance, preparation, and movement toward the bank, indicating a planned engagement with the institution.
memories.memory_text: I was part of a planned operation where we watched the bank, waited for the right moment, and got ready to move in together with Sal.

grounded_facts: Sal exits the car and starts walking toward the bank, marking the start of the planned action.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sal exit the car and start walking toward the bank, which meant it was time to move.

grounded_facts: After Sal begins moving, Sonny slowly gets out of the car, signaling escalation of the operation.
memories.memory_text: I slowly got out of the car after Sal, knowing this was the moment we escalated the operation.

grounded_facts: Howard asks Jackie whether he intends to enter or leave as the bank is closing.
memories.memory_text: I remember Howard asking Jackie whether he intended to enter or leave as the bank was closing.

grounded_facts: Sal sits down opposite Mulvaney and produces a machine pistol, holding it concealed against Mulvaney's chest.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sal sit down opposite Mulvaney and pull out a machine pistol, holding it concealed against his chest.

grounded_facts: Jackie tells Sonny he is getting bad vibes and suggests robbing a smaller place.
memories.memory_text: Jackie told me he was getting bad vibes and suggested we rob a smaller place, like a Spanish grocery.

grounded_facts: Initial phase of the bank robbery where Sal covertly takes control of the manager while Sonny and Jackie enter and position themselves.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Sal took control of the manager, and Jackie came over to me, clearly uneasy.

grounded_facts: Howard locks the bank door to prevent more customers from entering, marking the start of the robbery window.
memories.memory_text: I saw Howard unlock the door and hand a lollipop to the baby before she left, then lock the bank behind her.

grounded_facts: After confirming the bank is locked, Sonny rips open the florist box and aims a rifle at Sylvia Ball, the teller.
memories.memory_text: I confirmed the bank was locked and empty, so I crossed to the teller cage and ripped open the florist box, pulling out my rifle and aiming it at Sylvia Ball.

grounded_facts: Sonny shouts that it is a stickup, ordering everyone to freeze and move to the center of the bank.
memories.memory_text: I shouted that it was a stickup, telling everyone to freeze and move to the center of the bank so I could take control.

grounded_facts: The robbery becomes overt as Sonny reveals his rifle, announces the stickup, and commands staff to comply.
memories.memory_text: I revealed my rifle, aimed it at the teller, and shouted that this was a stickup, telling everyone to freeze and get away from their desks.

grounded_facts: Sonny instructs Jackie to shoot Howard if he moves, assigning him a violent role.
memories.memory_text: I told Jackie to shoot Howard if he moved, making it clear he had to cover him or things would go bad.

grounded_facts: When Sonny reports Jackie cannot go through with the robbery, Sal tells him to let Jackie leave.
memories.memory_text: I told Sal that Jackie couldn't make it, and Sal told me to let him go.

grounded_facts: Jackie, overwhelmed by fear, attempts to leave the bank during the robbery; Sonny allows him to exit after returning his gun.
memories.memory_text: Jackie started getting scared and told me he couldn't go through with it. I told the others to cover him, then reported to Sal that he couldn't make it. Sal said to let him go, so I made sure Jackie left safely, took his gun back, and locked the door behind him.

grounded_facts: Sonny insists on keeping the car, preventing Jackie from taking it, and successfully retrieves the keys.
Sonny forcefully asks Jackie to return the car keys, overriding Jackie's implied need for transportation.
memories.memory_text: I stopped Jackie from taking the car, told him to take the subway because we needed the car, and I made him hand over the keys—I had to be firm to keep control.

grounded_facts: After receiving the keys and Jackie's warning, Sonny turns back into the bank.
memories.memory_text: After I got the keys and heard Jackie's warning, I turned back into the bank myself.

grounded_facts: Jackie alerts Sonny to someone hiding under a desk inside the bank, just before leaving.
Jackie communicates an observation about someone under a desk inside the bank to Sonny.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Jackie that there's somebody under a desk inside the bank, just as he was leaving.

grounded_facts: Sonny orders Howard to pull the drapes, screening the bank's interior from outside view, creating a controlled environment.
memories.memory_text: I told Howard to pull the drapes so no one outside could see what was happening inside the bank.

grounded_facts: Sonny sprays red paint on all three security cameras to prevent recording or live monitoring of the robbery.
memories.memory_text: I sprayed red paint on all three security cameras to make sure they couldn't record us or let anyone watch from outside.

grounded_facts: Sonny stops Mulvaney from using a key with a spur that would trigger a silent alarm, asserting control over vault access.
Sonny physically intervenes and verbally threatens Mulvaney for attempting to use a key that would trigger a silent alarm.
memories.memory_text: I saw Mulvaney going to use that spur key, so I grabbed his hand and yelled at him—what the fuck was he thinking, trying to trip the alarm? I took the keys, showed him the one with the spur so he'd see it, then made him use the other one.

grounded_facts: Sonny carefully removes cash from teller drawers while avoiding alarm triggers, demonstrating knowledge of bank security systems.
memories.memory_text: I carefully took the cash from the teller drawers, making sure not to trigger any alarms—I knew exactly how the security systems worked and made sure Mulvaney used the right key without the spur.

grounded_facts: Sonny enters the vault and learns that most money was picked up earlier, leaving only a small amount behind.
memories.memory_text: I entered the vault and saw there was almost no money left — I yelled in frustration, searched for more, and realized it was just marked decoy bills; I couldn't believe what I was going to do with this tiny amount.

grounded_facts: Sonny imitates Sylvia’s voice while collecting money, asserting dominance through ridicule.
memories.memory_text: I mimicked Sylvia’s voice while collecting the money, just to assert control and show I wasn’t taking her seriously.

grounded_facts: An ongoing armed robbery led by Sonny inside a bank, involving hostage control, vault access, and theft preparation.
memories.memory_text: I was in charge of the whole robbery, making sure the hostages stayed under control, getting into the vault, and preparing to take the money without setting off any alarms.

grounded_facts: Sonny yells at Mulvaney while on the phone, warning him not to attempt deception, using Sal as an implied enforcer.
memories.memory_text: I yelled at Mulvaney over the phone, telling him not to play any games with me because I’m a Catholic and don’t want to hurt nobody, but then I made it clear I’d bark and Sal would bite if he tried anything.

grounded_facts: Sylvia requests Sonny moderate his language due to the presence of young girls.
memories.memory_text: Sylvia told me to watch my language because there were young girls around, but I didn’t feel like toning it down.

grounded_facts: Sonny burns the bank's transaction register to destroy evidence of the robbery's financial impact.
memories.memory_text: I told them to give me the register so I could burn it and destroy the evidence of how much was taken.

grounded_facts: After seeing Miriam cry uncontrollably, Sonny shifts tone and comforts her, denying intent to harm her.
memories.memory_text: I saw Miriam crying and it got to me, so I softened my tone and told her it wasn't her fault there was no money, asking her to please stop crying because I didn't want to hurt her.

grounded_facts: Sonny demands Howard's keys, signaling intent to leave the bank with hostages or escape vehicle.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Sonny demands Howard's keys, signaling intent to leave the bank with hostages or escape vehicle.

grounded_facts: Sonny uses calming language to reduce Howard's panic and gain cooperation in obtaining the keys.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Sonny uses calming language to reduce Howard's panic and gain cooperation in obtaining the keys.

grounded_facts: Sonny successfully acquires the keys from Howard after calming him down, enabling potential exit or escape planning.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Sonny successfully acquires the keys from Howard after calming him down, enabling potential exit or escape planning.

grounded_facts: Sonny stamps out the burning register to prevent further smoke emission that could attract outside attention.
memories.memory_text: I rushed to the smoking register and stamped it out to stop the smoke from drawing attention.

grounded_facts: Sal aims his gun at Sam, the approaching insurance agent, prepared to kill if necessary.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sal aim his gun at Sam, ready to shoot if he made a wrong move.

grounded_facts: Mulvaney unlocks and speaks with Sam, an insurance agent from across the street, to deflect suspicion about the robbery.
memories.memory_text: I watched Mulvaney talk to Sam at the door, making up a story about a cigarette, then handed me the keys after locking it again.

grounded_facts: Sylvia informs Sonny of her urgent need to use the bathroom due to fear of confinement.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sylvia telling me she had to go to the toilet and that she had a terrible fear of being locked in, so she couldn't hold it anymore.

grounded_facts: Sonny finds an additional person, Maria, in the ladies' room whom Sylvia had forgotten, expanding the hostage count.
memories.memory_text: I found Maria sitting in the ladies' room, painting her nails and listening to a radio, completely unaware. I yelled, 'Who the hell is that?' when I saw her, and Sylvia admitted she had forgotten Maria was even there.

grounded_facts: Sonny orders Sal to move all hostages into the vault, securing them in a confined, controllable space.
memories.memory_text: I told Sal to get all the hostages into the vault so we could keep control, and I helped herd them in, making sure the last ones went through before locking it up.

grounded_facts: Sonny answers a phone call from Detective Sergeant Moretti, who reveals police surveillance and control over the situation.
Detective Moretti asserts dominance by informing Sonny that he is under full surveillance and in police control.
memories.memory_text: I took the phone from Mulvaney and said 'Yeah,' and then Detective Moretti told me he had me completely by the balls, that he was watching me right now and could see me in the bank.

grounded_facts: Sonny sees a detective across the street on the phone and receives a call from Moretti, confirming that the police are monitoring the bank.
memories.memory_text: I looked out and saw a detective across the street on the phone in the barbershop window, watching us. Then Moretti called me directly, confirming the police are monitoring the bank and telling me to surrender calmly.

grounded_facts: Moretti speaks to Sonny on the phone, positioning himself as the controlling authority and urging compliance.
memories.memory_text: Moretti spoke to me on the phone, trying to position himself as the one in control, telling me to be reasonable and surrender without causing trouble.

grounded_facts: Sonny issues a threat over the phone to start throwing bodies out unless police stay away, intending to deter approach.
memories.memory_text: I told the police over the phone that if they don't stay away from the bank, we'll start throwing bodies out one at a time. I said it loud and clear so they'd know I mean business.

grounded_facts: Sonny softens his tone when Jenny asks what to tell her husband, showing empathy for her fear.
memories.memory_text: I saw how scared Jenny was when she asked what to tell her husband, so I softened my voice and told her to say whatever she needed to say — I even told her to tell him I don't know, just to ease her fear.

grounded_facts: Jenny takes a personal call from her husband, revealing domestic normalcy amid crisis and confirming hostages' access to communication.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jenny's husband on the phone asking when she'd be home, and I listened as she talked to him about cooking and the baby, ending with 'I love you' before she hung up and walked away.

grounded_facts: Sonny tells police he will throw bodies out unless they stay back, but privately admits he doesn't intend to follow through.
memories.memory_text: I told the police we'd start throwing bodies out unless they stayed back, but afterward I admitted to Sal that I don't actually intend to do it—I just need them to believe I will so they keep their distance.

grounded_facts: Sonny expresses guilt for involving Sal and reassures him they can survive the situation.
memories.memory_text: I felt bad for pulling Sal into this, so I apologized and told him we can get through it together, that we won’t have to throw anyone out.

grounded_facts: Sonny addresses all hostages, promising safety through cooperation and access to basic needs like bathroom and phone use.
memories.memory_text: I told everyone that if we all cooperate and stay calm, things are going to be all right, and I promised they’d get to use the bathroom and the phone when they needed to.

grounded_facts: Sonny questions Mulvaney and then tasks him with checking escape routes, establishing a working relationship.
memories.memory_text: I questioned the guy, found out his name was Mulvaney, and told him we were checking the escape routes together before heading to the back door.

grounded_facts: Sonny and Mulvaney move a heavy office machine to barricade the back door, preparing for potential police entry.
memories.memory_text: I worked with Mulvaney to push a heavy machine toward the back door to block it, straining and laughing as we got it into place to keep the police out.

grounded_facts: Sonny declares his intention to take a married female hostage with children as a human shield, believing police will be less likely to use force against such a target.
memories.memory_text: I decided I'm going to take one of the married women with kids as a hostage because the cops won't risk shooting her—nobody wants to see a mother die in the papers.

grounded_facts: After using Mulvaney to help block the back door, Sonny allows him to put his jacket back on, signaling a minor restoration of dignity or status.
memories.memory_text: I let Mulvaney put his jacket back on after we finished blocking the back door, and then we walked back together toward Sal and the others.

grounded_facts: Sonny compliments Mulvaney as a 'nice guy' but issues a veiled threat not to 'fuck around,' establishing boundaries of acceptable behavior.
memories.memory_text: I told Mulvaney he's a nice guy, but I made it clear he shouldn't fuck around with me—I need him to know the line.

grounded_facts: Sonny puts all phone receivers back on hooks, preparing for communication with police.
memories.memory_text: I put all the phone receivers back on the hooks to get ready to talk to the police.

grounded_facts: Sonny and Moretti begin verbal negotiation; identities and basic terms are exchanged.
memories.memory_text: I started talking with Moretti, and he wanted to know who I was and how many people were in the bank; I told him to call me Sonny-boy, and he asked if he could call me Sonny instead, which I said was fine.

grounded_facts: Moretti asks Sonny to release women as a sign of goodwill.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Moretti that he wanted to see if the people in the bank were okay, and then he asked me to let them out, saying they shouldn't be in that position.

grounded_facts: Initial phase of communication between hostage-takers and police, establishing terms and testing trust.
memories.memory_text: I reconnected the phones and started talking with Moretti. He asked about the hostages and how many were inside, then wanted to know my name. I told him to call me Sonny-boy, and when he asked if he could call me Sonny instead, I said he could call me whatever he wanted. He proposed coming over unarmed so I could frisk him to prove trust, but I made it clear the hostages are what's keeping me alive. After some back and forth, I agreed to send one out to see what I could do.

grounded_facts: Sonny agrees to release one hostage to demonstrate good faith in negotiations.
memories.memory_text: I agreed to release one hostage alive as a sign of good faith during the negotiations, and after talking with Sal, we decided to send out the guard.

grounded_facts: Howard is pushed out of the bank and immediately seized by police under aggressive conditions.
Cops respond to Howard's exit with overwhelming force, mistaking him for a perpetrator.
memories.memory_text: I saw the cops rush Howard the moment he came out, shoving him against a car and bending him over like he was some kind of criminal, and I realized they had no idea what was really going on—I didn't expect them to react that violently.

grounded_facts: Moretti invites Sonny outside to see the overwhelming police and media presence.
memories.memory_text: Moretti called me out, saying, 'Sonny - come out here a minute,' and then urged me to come see something.

grounded_facts: Sonny refuses to come out unless police stand back, citing Sal's threat to kill hostages.
memories.memory_text: I told Moretti he couldn't expect me to come out because Sal's back there with the girls, and if anything happens to me, he'll kill them.

grounded_facts: Sonny steps outside with Sylvia and sees the full scale of police and media presence.
memories.memory_text: I stepped outside with Sylvia, and as I looked around, I realized I was completely surrounded and had become an event—crowds cheering, cops with guns aimed at me.

grounded_facts: Sonny realizes Moretti cannot deliver a real deal and demands to speak with someone in authority, exposing the negotiation's futility.
Sonny ridicules Moretti's attempt to negotiate, accusing him of being a powerless 'flunky pig'.
memories.memory_text: I realized Moretti couldn't offer me any real deal, so I called him out—he's just a city cop pretending to have power, a flunky pig trying to bullshit me, and I demanded to speak with someone actually in charge.

grounded_facts: Sonny blames the media for preventing a massacre, implying their presence stops police from killing hostages.
memories.memory_text: I told them that if it wasn't for the media, the police would've killed everyone and blamed it on me and Sal.

grounded_facts: Sonny's public defiance and demand to lower weapons forces Moretti to order the police to stand down.
memories.memory_text: I told Moretti to get the guns lowered because I couldn't stand seeing them pointed at me, and I saw him gesture for the officers to back down, so I knew I had control.

grounded_facts: Sonny turns to cameras and waves, playing to the media and crowd after gaining symbolic victory.
After the police lower their weapons, Sonny is cheered by the crowd and begins performing for the media.
memories.memory_text: I turned to the cameras and waved, playing to the crowd after realizing they were cheering and that I had control of the moment.

grounded_facts: Vi's husband tries to turn off the television during the news coverage, but Vi stops him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vi stop her husband from turning off the TV while they were watching the news coverage.

grounded_facts: Sonny holds the bank door open for Sylvia, showing patience and allowing her to reenter.
memories.memory_text: I held the door open for Sylvia, waiting for her to decide whether to go back in.

grounded_facts: Sylvia decides to reenter the bank despite being told to stay out, asserting her commitment to the hostages inside.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sylvia walk past me and into the bank, even though she was told to stay out, because she cared about the hostages.

grounded_facts: Moretti yells at the media to leave and simultaneously gives an operational order to a nearby cop.
memories.memory_text: I saw Moretti yelling at the media to get away while he turned and gave an order to a cop nearby.

grounded_facts: Moretti gives an order to turn off the air conditioning inside the bank, likely to pressure the hostages or robbers.
memories.memory_text: I figured Moretti was trying to pressure the people inside the bank when he ordered the air conditioning to be turned off.

grounded_facts: An ongoing crisis situation at the bank involving hostages and law enforcement presence, with media and crowd gathered outside.
memories.memory_text: I was there with Moretti, the media was shouting, cops were getting orders, and when I turned, the crowd was applauding and I waved back.

grounded_facts: Mulvaney turns on the TV set upon Sonny's request, enabling the media broadcast to be seen inside the bank.
memories.memory_text: I told Mulvaney to turn on the TV, and he did, so we could see the broadcast inside the bank.

grounded_facts: The TV newsman initiates a phone call through the bank manager to speak directly with Sonny, marking the beginning of live media negotiation.
memories.memory_text: I was told the TV people wanted to talk to me, and Mulvaney handed me the phone so I could speak directly with the newsman.

grounded_facts: A live television news broadcast captures the bank interior and establishes a phone link between the newsman and Sonny, turning the robbery into a public spectacle.
memories.memory_text: I saw the news broadcast showing us inside the bank, and I heard the newsman say we were on the air and robbing the bank, making it feel like we were being watched by everyone.

grounded_facts: Sonny challenges the newsman about media exploitation, asserting that he and Sal are being used as entertainment while facing death.
Sonny denounces the newsman for treating the crisis as entertainment while refusing to engage with his humanity or material needs.
memories.memory_text: I challenged the newsman on air, telling him we weren't just entertainment for his audience—we're people facing death, and he wouldn't even answer my questions about what he makes or how we might survive.

grounded_facts: The live transmission is abruptly cut off, ending the media-robber dialogue.
memories.memory_text: I remember hanging up the phone and looking at Mulvaney, confused, after the broadcast was suddenly cut off and the announcer said they were interrupting the transmission.

grounded_facts: Sal refuses Sonny's suggestion of negotiating a plea deal, reaffirming a prior suicide pact.
memories.memory_text: I suggested to Sal that we could negotiate a plea deal to get out alive, but he refused and reminded me of our suicide pact, saying he'd never go back to prison.

grounded_facts: An anonymous caller instructs Sonny to kill all hostages immediately.
memories.memory_text: I walked over to the phone when it rang, picked it up, and heard someone tell me to kill all the hostages—I told them to fuck off and never call again.

grounded_facts: Sonny shifts strategy from surrender to international escape, requesting a helicopter and jet to flee to the Caribbean or Algeria.
Sonny promises the hostages they will survive if they continue cooperating.
memories.memory_text: After Sal shut down the idea of a deal, I shifted my plan and told the hostages we're all going to get out alive if they keep cooperating, and I demanded a helicopter and a jet to escape to the Caribbean or Algeria.

grounded_facts: Sonny complies with Sal's request and gives him the rifle before exiting toward the front door.
memories.memory_text: I gave my rifle to Sal when he asked for it, then started moving toward the front door.

grounded_facts: A man identified as Maria's boyfriend suddenly attacks Sonny, beating him before being restrained by police, revealing public hostility and emotional volatility surrounding the standoff.
memories.memory_text: I was completely taken by surprise when a man came running at me from the crowd and knocked me to the ground, beating me before anyone could stop him.

grounded_facts: Moretti ridicules Maria's boyfriend for taking vigilante action, dismissing his emotional motivation and asserting institutional control.
memories.memory_text: I saw Moretti mock the man who attacked me, ridiculing him for trying to take action, and it reinforced how little control any of us really have out there.

grounded_facts: Sonny reports that Sal intended to kill him upon seeing him, indicating a shift in internal dynamics among the hostage-takers and increasing Sonny's perceived vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I told them that Sal wanted to kill me when he saw me — I could see it in his eyes, and it made me feel completely exposed.

grounded_facts: Sonny demands a helicopter and a large international jet with specific amenities to facilitate escape, marking a strategic escalation in his negotiation stance.
memories.memory_text: I demanded a helicopter and a big international jet with a bar and a piano lounge so we could get out of the country safely.

grounded_facts: Sonny demands that his wife be brought to the bank, introducing a personal stake into the negotiation and potentially altering leverage dynamics.
memories.memory_text: I told them I want to see my wife and for them to bring her down here, because I need her with me now.

grounded_facts: An ongoing armed standoff at a bank where Sonny and accomplices are holding hostages, with police negotiation and media presence.
memories.memory_text: I stepped out during the standoff, demanding a helicopter and a jet to get out of the country, and I made it clear I wanted to see my wife before anything else.

grounded_facts: Moretti proposes exchanging Sonny's wife for female hostages, introducing a quid pro quo structure to the negotiation.

grounded_facts: Sonny asks Mulvaney hypothetically if he would hire him, revealing a desire for normalcy and redemption, though he dismisses it as implausible.

grounded_facts: Sylvia asks for a cigarette and expresses despair about her future, sarcastically noting she already knows who her husband will marry after her death.
memories.memory_text: I heard Sylvia ask for another cigarette and then say she already knows who her husband will marry after she dies, which made me feel a pang of sadness for her.

grounded_facts: Jenny identifies that Mulvaney used the 'F' word, which becomes the catalyst for the group's laughter.

grounded_facts: Edna declares her ears are not 'garbage cans' as a Christian, rejecting profanity and reigniting laughter.

grounded_facts: After Mulvaney apologizes for using the 'F' word, the hostages erupt in uncontrollable laughter, a release of built-up tension.
memories.memory_text: I was there when the whole group suddenly burst into uncontrollable laughter after Mulvaney’s apology, and I felt the tension break all at once, like we were all in it together for a moment.

grounded_facts: Sonny's mother appears outside the bank, escorted by police, and Sheldon calls for Sonny to come out via bullhorn.

grounded_facts: Vi pressures Sonny to give himself up, citing FBI assurances and family support, undermining his escape plan.

grounded_facts: Sonny becomes aware that his conversation with his mother is diverting him from the urgent situation, as has happened before, and attempts to refocus.

grounded_facts: Sonny forcefully denies his mother's explanation that Heidi caused his actions, asserting his autonomy and identity.
memories.memory_text: I told my mother she was wrong to blame Heidi for my actions—I made it clear that this is who I am, not something caused by my marriage.

grounded_facts: A private, emotionally charged meeting between Sonny and his mother outside the bank during the standoff, under police lights and public attention.
memories.memory_text: I remember standing outside the bank with my mother under those bright lights, everyone watching, and me trying to keep it together while she poured out all her fears and demands.

grounded_facts: Sonny delivers a self-condemning monologue about his destructive impact on those he loves, framing himself as inherently harmful.
memories.memory_text: I said out loud that I'm a fuckup and an outcast, and that everyone I love gets hurt because of me—I truly believe that if I love someone, they're going to get destroyed.

memories.memory_text: I was in the limo with Sal when we roared through the airport gate just as a guard swung it open, and I knew we were making our escape as the pursuing cars crashed into the gate behind us.

grounded_facts: Maria gives her rosary to Sal, comforting him about his first plane trip, showing maternal care.
memories.memory_text: I saw Maria give her rosary to Sal, telling him not to be scared about his first plane trip, which felt like she was comforting him like a mother would.

grounded_facts: Sal smiles and tells Sonny 'You did it!', expressing pride and belief in their escape.

grounded_facts: The FBI agents, led by Sheldon, execute their plan by having the driver turn with a gun and open fire, resulting in Sal's death and Sonny's capture.
memories.memory_text: I think I realized too late that the FBI wasn't going along with the deal — Sheldon moved fast, disarmed me, and the driver turned with a gun, like they'd planned it all along.

grounded_facts: Sal is shot twice by the FBI driver and dies instantly, marking the collapse of the escape plan and Sonny's emotional devastation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sal get hit twice — the first shot threw him back, and the second snapped his head back as he stared at me, upside down, like he knew it was coming, like he felt betrayed. Then he just... died, right in front of me.

grounded_facts: A planned exchange where the FBI appears to comply with the captors' demands, culminating in a takedown.
memories.memory_text: I was part of the exchange where the FBI seemed to go along with our demands, I asked Sal if he was ready to go, and then everything fell apart when I saw Sheldon grab my rifle and agents swarmed us.

grounded_facts: After surviving, Sylvia kisses Mulvaney passionately, expressing long-suppressed desire.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sylvia kiss Mulvaney hard, and she said she'd been waiting years to do it — he kissed her back while laughing.

grounded_facts: The surviving hostages, including Sylvia and Mulvaney, are freed and react with emotional relief, hugging and kissing.
memories.memory_text: I saw the hostages get out of the limo, hugging and crying, just overwhelmed with relief that they were alive.

grounded_facts: Sheldon formally places Sonny under arrest after disarming him.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Sheldon formally places Sonny under arrest after disarming him.

memories.memory_text: I remember that After Sal's death, Sonny is disarmed and formally placed under arrest by Sheldon.

grounded_facts: Text overlay reveals Sonny is serving a 25-year federal prison sentence, confirming the legal consequence of his actions.
memories.memory_text: I heard during the credits that I was serving a 25-year federal prison sentence, the consequence of everything that went down.

grounded_facts: Pauline reveals she only learned of her son Sal's involvement and death from television news, indicating emotional distance and lack of prior contact.
memories.memory_text: I heard about Sal's involvement and death on the TV, just like everyone else, and it hit me hard because I hadn't known he was even involved.

grounded_facts: Pauline states she did not know Sal was homosexual until after his death.
memories.memory_text: I didn't know Sal was homosexual until after they killed him, and I learned that truth too late to say anything at all.

grounded_facts: Sonny witnesses Sal's body being carried past him, marking the finality of Sal's death and intensifying Sonny's isolation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sal's body being carried past me, and I knew it was over — he was really gone, and I felt completely alone.

grounded_facts: FBI agent orders Sonny to keep his eyes forward, preventing him from seeing Sal's body.
memories.memory_text: I tried to look at Sal as they carried him past, but an FBI agent told me to keep my eyes front, so I couldn't even see him one last time.

grounded_facts: The hostages are released and begin to return home, marking the formal end of the hostage situation.
memories.memory_text: I watched the hostages start to leave, heading back to their lives, while I stayed behind, frozen in place.

grounded_facts: Sonny calls out affectionately to the hostages as they leave, calling them 'terrific' and 'beautiful'.
memories.memory_text: I called out to the hostages as they were leaving, telling them they were terrific and beautiful, and I meant every word.

grounded_facts: The hostages pass Sonny on their way home, offering only perfunctory goodbyes, signaling the end of their shared experience and Sonny's emotional isolation.
memories.memory_text: I saw the hostages pass by me on their way home, and though I reached out, their goodbyes felt forced and distant, like we were no longer part of the same story.

grounded_facts: Sal checks his appearance, adjusting his tie and cuffs, showing readiness for the upcoming activity at the bank.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sal checking his tie and adjusting his cuffs in the car, getting himself ready for what was about to happen at the bank.

memories.memory_text: I watched Jackie get out of the car and walk over to the bank window to look inside.

memories.memory_text: I had a fake conversation with Jackie when he returned to the car, and I could tell he was relaying what he saw inside the bank.

grounded_facts: Sal exits the car and begins walking toward the bank, marking the start of the operation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sal exit the car and start walking toward the bank, so I knew it was time to begin the operation.

grounded_facts: Sonny slowly gets out of the car, following Sal's movement toward the bank.
memories.memory_text: I slowly got out of the car right after Sal, following him toward the bank.

grounded_facts: A coordinated operation in which Sonny, Sal, and Jackie position themselves near a bank in preparation for a heist.
memories.memory_text: I was watching everything come together near the bank—Jackie came back after checking the window, Sal got ready, and I knew it was time for us to move into position as part of the plan.

grounded_facts: Jackie tells Sonny he is getting bad vibes and suggests robbing a smaller place.

grounded_facts: Mulvaney yells at Sylvia to confirm they understand it's a stickup, reacting to Sonny's outburst.
memories.memory_text: I heard Mulvaney yell to Sylvia that they knew it was a stickup, reacting to my outburst.

memories.memory_text: I saw that Howard wasn't doing anything useful, so I grabbed his keys and locked the front door to make sure no one could get out.

grounded_facts: An armed robbery of a small branch bank initiated by Sal, Sonny, and Jackie, though Jackie withdraws early.

memories.memory_text: I was told by Jackie that there's somebody under a desk inside the bank.
